static_traits.name: Li Ting
static_traits.family_status: No children, lives alone in the countryside
static_traits.social_status: Interpersonal relationships are strained due to the recent divorce, feels isolated; has a few distant relatives who occasionally care, but lacks close friends
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar psychological problems in the past, has not received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly with a negative tone, able to cooperate in exploring thoughts; tends to ruminate over negative memories and self-negation

basic_info.main_problem: After a recent divorce, I feel I have been a failure my whole life; these feelings of failure occur almost daily and have made me lose enjoyment in gardening, which I once loved.
basic_info.core_demands: Hopes to deal with feelings of failure and rebuild a sense of self-worth.
growth_experiences: The divorce a few months ago: the spouse proposed divorce completely unexpectedly, and the stress was extreme when it happened. After the divorce, the client ruminated daily on negative thoughts, treating previously unachieved goals as proof of their own failure; gardening no longer brought joy, and overall mood and well-being declined; interpersonal relationships became strained because of the divorce, and the client felt isolated, with only a few distant relatives occasionally showing concern.

special_situations.event: Recalling the relationship with ex-husband and the divorce process (especially being unexpectedly divorced)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If marriage fails, it proves my whole life is a failure.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly replays relationship details, searching for own faults to gain explanation and a sense of control.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I have been a failure my whole life; it is all my fault.

special_situations.event: Recalling a period when the partner worked overtime for weeks in a row and they barely communicated
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I had not done more at that time, his leaving is because of me.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Uses 'I should have done more' as a rule for after-the-fact self-blame, trying to make up for it by demanding twice as much of the self.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should have done more; I caused the divorce.

special_situations.event: When reflecting on past achievements and unachieved goals
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not achieved enough, it amounts to failure.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries to suppress feelings of failure with distracting activities (reading, painting, gardening), but persistently focuses with negative filtering on unfinished parts.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I have not achieved anything, so I am a failure.

special_situations.event: In the garden or while gardening, finds the enjoyment has disappeared
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am a real failure, I do not deserve to enjoy things I like.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reluctantly continues the activity to distract attention, but emotional reasoning quickly reduces engagement and enjoyment.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never feel joy from gardening again.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to maintain intimacy and to be cherished and understood
core_conflict.fear: Afraid of being abandoned and proven worthless, a failure
defense_goal: Maintains a controllable explanatory framework through self-blame and taking full responsibility, reducing anxiety about uncontrollable loss

object_relations.object_representation: Representing a significant other (ex-husband) as a 'busy and distant person'

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes a more balanced perspective or alternative explanation, inviting joint examination of the evidence
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Worries that exploration will confirm 'it is all my fault', experiencing the process of understanding as possible blame and accusation (self-directed transference)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Hesitant tone, repeats self-blaming questions (such as 'what if it really is my fault'), seeks certainty and evidence, and reduces emotional exposure.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about 'whether it is not all my fault' and responsibility attribution issues
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes that only by finding conclusive evidence can they allow themselves to reduce self-blame, using rational analysis to avoid touching painful emotions
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Requests that facts and evidence be listed, leans toward analysis and attribution discussion, with a cautious tone and restrained emotional expression.

manifestations: No children, lives alone in the countryside
Interpersonal relationships strained due to divorce, lacking close friends to confide in
outcomes: Low mood与Decline in sense of well-being

manifestations: Ruminating on the past and viewing unachieved goals as a lifetime of failure

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently uses the self-requirement 'I should have done more' to explain the relationship rupture
Directly adopts the external standard of 'success means valuable, failure means worthless' as the basis for self-evaluation

contact_model.definition: The individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Turning the energy of relationship loss and dissatisfaction inward into self-blame and rumination
Reducing seeking help externally and expressing needs, tending to repeatedly examine oneself internally

positive_force: Proactively seeking and starting psychological counseling, willing to cooperate with reality testing
Able to identify and describe one's own negative automatic thoughts
Past behaviors of giving support and care in the relationship
Retaining a foundation of interests such as gardening, reading, painting (though affected)
negative_force: Tendencies toward catastrophizing and all-or-nothing thinking
Personalization attribution and labeling oneself a 'failure'
Negatively screening past achievements, negating the positive side
Weak social support and a subjective sense of isolation
Persistent rumination over memories of a past relationship causes emotional distress

target_behavior.behavior: Persistent self-negation and sense of failure (occurring almost daily)
antecedent: Recalling the relationship with the ex-husband and the course of the divorce
Reflecting on past achievements and unachieved goals
target_behavior.core_reason: The suddenness of the divorce triggers overgeneralizing and personalizing cognitions, regarding the relationship breakdown as a failure of the whole life and attributing it to one's own fault.
target_behavior.function: Obtains a false sense of control and an explanatory framework through self-blame, in order to avoid facing external uncontrollable factors and a sense of loss.
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood, anhedonia, decreased interest in activities such as gardening, and further interpersonal estrangement.

target_behavior.behavior: Reduced activity participation / loss of interest in gardening
antecedent: When thinking about the divorce event or relationship memories
When gardening, associating with past relationships and periods of no communication
target_behavior.core_reason: Emotional reasoning and negative filtering: because of feeling like a failure, concludes the activity is meaningless and finds it hard to obtain joy from it.
target_behavior.function: Avoiding triggering painful memories and negative emotions, reducing emotional activation in the short term.
target_behavior.consequence: Daily functioning and well-being decline; quality of life is impaired.
